name: Software Development
tagline: Build the applications Rwanda runs on
summary: Learn to design, code and ship real software — from your first web page to a full database-driven application.
description: Software Development is one of the flagship trades at Lycée de Nyanza. Students spend most of their week in the computer lab, working on live projects in small teams: school management tools, mobile-first websites, simple games and data dashboards. Alongside the code, the trade teaches version control, testing, documentation and the professional habits employers expect.
entry_requirements: Senior 3 (or L3 entry) with a pass in Mathematics and English. No previous coding experience is required — students who bring a laptop of their own are encouraged to do so.

modules: Team projects with Git and code review

name: Networking & Internet Technology
summary: Design, install and secure the networks that every school, bank and office depends on.
description: Networking & Internet Technology trains students to build and maintain the physical and wireless networks behind modern organisations. The trade lab holds routers, switches, structured cabling kits and a small server rack, so learners practice on real equipment rather than diagrams alone.
entry_requirements: Senior 3 (or L3 entry) with a pass in Mathematics and Physics. Curiosity about how the internet works matters more than prior experience.
